question: Through which of the following body parts does food need to pass before reaching the intestines?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Oesophagus → Stomach**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **oesophagus**, also known as the **food pipe**, is a muscular tube that connects the throat (pharynx) with the stomach.
 
• After food is chewed and swallowed, it passes through the **oesophagus** to reach the **stomach**.
 
• The **stomach** is a muscular organ located on the left side of the upper abdomen. It receives food from the **oesophagus**.
 
• In the stomach, food is mixed with digestive juices and broken down into a semi-liquid form called **chyme**.
 
• The **chyme** then moves into the small intestine for further digestion and nutrient absorption.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Windpipe → Food pipe**__

 __
 
• The **windpipe**, or trachea, is part of the respiratory system and is not involved in the digestive process.
 
• It carries air to the lungs, while the food pipe (oesophagus) carries food to the stomach.
 
 
 
• **Mouth → Rectum**__
 __
 
• Food does pass through the mouth, but the rectum is the last part of the digestive system, not an intermediate step before the intestines.
 
• The rectum is involved in the excretion of waste, not in the digestion of food.
 
 
 
• **Stomach → Rectum**__
 
 
• Food passes through several other parts of the digestive system before reaching the rectum, including the small and large intestines.
 
• The rectum stores feces until they are expelled from the body.
